newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel says GDP to grow under 4.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel says GDP to grow under 4.0 pct.

text.p: Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel said on Monday that gross domestic product (GDP) would grow less than the projected 4.0 percent for 1997 but expressed confidence the Treasury would keep to its budget deficit target.

Treasury officials have hinted in recent days that they may be willing to let the deficit exceed the target because of a slowing economy but Frenkel warned at a news conference that it would lead to a loss of credibility.
"It will be below the four percent that was put into the budget, but it is too early to come up with a precise estimate," Frenkel said at a news conference unveiling the central bank's annual report.

Private sector economists have forecast growth of less than four percent but the Treasury has so far kept to its original estimates. Frenkel said containing the budget deficit was a key element "to make sure this slowdown remains shallow and brief."

"I take the government's statement that it means business," he said. "When it says it's going to try to reach its targets as far as the budget is concerned I take it seriously. Of course if we don't see that effort realised there will be room for concern because there will be basically two issues -- one, a loss of credibility and second, a loss for the economy."

The 1997 budget calls for a target deficit of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product but exceeded the target in the first quarter, according to Treasury estimates. Last week the Treasury's outgoing director-general David Brodett said keeping exactly to the target was not critical, especially in a slowing economy. But Frenkel said: "I think at the present stage it would be a mistake to decide policies intentionally to miss targets."
